name: mgen
title: viva-Mgen: reproducing the Karr 2012 M. genitalium whole-cell model, one study per figure
description:
Seven studies, one per figure of Karr et al. 2012, all built on the same
viva-native reproduction of the whole-cell model (package viva_mgen). The
metabolic engine is the real published Suthers 2009 iPS189 reconstruction
(351 reactions, 126 genes) solved with cobra; mass, cell-cycle, and
composition constants are taken verbatim from the original model's fitted
parameters. Fidelity is honest and per-study: Fig 2 (growth/composition) and
Fig 6 (metabolic-gene essentiality) are full-fidelity; Fig 4 is a genuine but
reduced mechanism; Fig 1/3/5/7 are representative/reduced. Each study has a
real expected_behavior/behavior_tests pair, a canonical sims/run.py that
drives the composite and renders an interactive visualization, and a run
recorded in the workspace .pbg/runs.jsonl. See each study's own fidelity note
and caveats. This is NOT the full 28-submodel model (chromosome occupancy,
128-cell population distributions, and the 3,011-strain deletion scan are out
of scope) — it is a reduced-but-genuine core, faithful where it claims to be.
question:
Can the core cellular processes of the Karr et al. 2012 Mycoplasma genitalium
whole-cell model be re-expressed as native process-bigraph Processes —
composed through shared cell-variable stores — and reproduce the central
quantitative results of each figure of the paper?
hypothesis:
A reduced-but-genuine set of viva-native submodels — FBA metabolism over the
published iPS189 reconstruction, calibrated mass/growth, stochastic
transcription/translation/decay, and a dNTP-buffered replication process —
wired together as one process-bigraph composite is sufficient to recapitulate
the paper's headline phenotypes: a ~9 h doubling time and protein-dominant
composition (Fig 2), decoupled mRNA/protein expression (Fig 2G/3), the
emergent inverse initiation↔replication cell-cycle control (Fig 4), an
ATP/GTP-dominated energy budget led by translation (Fig 5), and metabolic
gene-essentiality prediction near the published accuracy (Fig 6), plus a
sigmoidal growth-vs-kinetic-parameter response (Fig 7).

executive.what_is_this:
A showcase investigation that reproduces the landmark Karr 2012 whole-cell
model of M. genitalium as native process-bigraph processes, with one study
for each of the paper's seven figures. It demonstrates that the model's
central results — 9 h doubling, protein-dominant composition, decoupled
gene expression, emergent cell-cycle regulation, ATP/GTP energy allocation,
and metabolic gene essentiality — are recoverable from a compact, genuinely
mechanistic reimplementation, without the original's MATLAB code, MySQL
knowledge base, or cluster-scale simulation.
executive.verdict:
All seven studies are authored, lint-clean, and executable, each with a real
@composite_generator baseline, a sims/run.py canonical runner, an interactive
visualization, and a completed run recorded in .pbg/runs.jsonl. Standalone
execution reproduces the paper's results at the stated fidelity: doubling
time 9.00 h / mass ×2.00 / protein 62.0% (fig2, full); mRNA↔protein
decoupling with a protein:mRNA ratio ~180 (fig3, reduced); inverse
initiation↔replication control r=-0.93 and dNTP↔replication r=-0.95 across
128 cells (fig4, reduced mechanism); ATP:GTP synthesis ratio 4.03 with
translation taking ~97% of the modeled expression-energy budget (fig5,
reduced); metabolic gene-essentiality accuracy 76.0% over 125 genes with a
confusion matrix [[80,26],[4,15]] vs the paper's 79% / iPS189's 87% (fig6,
full for metabolic genes); and the six submodels integrate through shared
stores into one viable cell (fig1). The PASS/FAIL verdicts here come from
each runner's own printed checks against the study's expected_behavior, not
(yet) from the dashboard's Tests-tab evaluator.
executive.verdict_detail:
Done: all 7 studies authored + run + visualized, runs in .pbg/runs.jsonl,
read-only workbench published. Not done: driving the recorded runs through
the dashboard's Tests-tab evaluator (the verdicts above are the runner
scripts' own checks); expanding the reduced studies toward full fidelity
(full gene set for expression/t50, chromosome occupancy for Fig 3,
128-cell populations for Fig 2B/5, the full 3,011-strain deletion scan).

scientific_argument.main_claim:
The core quantitative results of the Karr 2012 whole-cell model are
reproducible by a reduced-but-genuine, fully viva-native reimplementation:
real FBA over iPS189 plus calibrated mass/growth reproduce the growth,
composition, energy, and essentiality figures at full or near-full fidelity,
and compact mechanistic submodels reproduce the emergent cell-cycle-control
and expression-decoupling phenomena qualitatively.
evidence_for: fig2 (FULL): FBA-driven growth calibrated to the fitted cell cycle gives a doubling time of 9.00 h, mass doubling of 2.00× per cycle, and a protein-dominant dry-mass composition of 62.0% — matching Fig 2A/B/C.

fig6 (FULL, metabolic subset): in-silico single-gene FBA knockouts over the 125 iPS189 metabolic genes classify essentiality at 76.0% accuracy (sensitivity 0.755, specificity 0.789; confusion matrix [[80,26],[4,15]]), in the neighborhood of the paper's 79% whole-cell and iPS189's 87% metabolic accuracy (Fig 6A).

fig4 (reduced mechanism): across 128 single cells, replication-initiation and replication durations are inversely correlated (r=-0.930), dNTP-at-start vs replication duration r=-0.951, and initial DnaA vs initiation duration r=-0.743 — reproducing the emergent, genetically-unregulated cell-cycle control of Fig 4C/D/E via genuine dNTP-surplus buffering.

fig5 (reduced): ATP and GTP dominate energy synthesis (ATP:GTP flux ratio 4.03), and translation takes ~96.8% of the modeled transcription+translation energy budget — reproducing the translation-led ordering of Fig 5A/5D.

fig3 (reduced): stochastic expression on the representative gene panel yields bursty low-copy mRNA (~1.7 mean copies/gene) and much higher, stabler protein (protein:mRNA ~180), reproducing the mRNA/protein decoupling of Fig 2G/2H.

fig1 (representative): the six submodels (metabolism, mass, transcription, translation, RNA decay, protein decay) integrate through shared cell-variable stores into a single viable, growing cell — the process-bigraph analog of the paper's Fig 1 integration diagram.

fig7 (reduced): predicted growth depends on a metabolic reaction's flux bound (a kcat/Vmax proxy) with a monotonic, saturating (sigmoidal) response — reproducing the growth-vs-kinetic-parameter relationship of Fig 7E–G. (See the fig7 study for the target reaction and dynamic range.)
evidence_against: This is a reduced core, not the full 28-submodel model: chromosome-level DNA–protein interactions and occupancy (the actual subject of Fig 3), 128-cell population distributions (Fig 2B, 4A, 5B), and the full 3,011-strain single-gene deletion scan (Fig 6/7) are not reproduced.
Gene essentiality is assessed only for the ~125 metabolic genes iPS189 covers, not all 525 genes; the paper's whole-cell essentiality spans non-metabolic genes this reproduction does not model.

Expression uses a 6-gene representative panel with representative rates, so the quantitative Fig 3C timing (t50 ≈ 18 min over all genes) is out of scope; only the qualitative bursty-mRNA / accumulating-protein decoupling is reproduced.
Fig 7's kinetic parameter is a flux-bound proxy for kcat, not explicit enzyme kinetics; the specific lpdA/deoD/thyA genetics of the paper are not individually modeled.
caveats: Behavior-test verdicts are the runner scripts' own printed checks against each study's expected_behavior; they have not yet been driven through the dashboard's Tests-tab evaluator.

The metabolic growth flux is calibrated (via growth_fraction) so unperturbed growth doubles the cell in the fitted 9 h; the FBA sets the RELATIVE growth that gene disruptions and kinetic changes then modulate.

studies.name: parca-parameter-fitting
studies.title: ParCa — parameter fitting (Karr 2012 FitConstants reproduction)
studies.question: Can viva-Mgen reproduce Karr 2012's parameter calculator (FitConstants) — computing the per-gene expression, decay and synthesis parameters the whole-cell model runs on from the real observed knowledge-base data, rather than hand-tuned guesses — and are those fitted parameters metabolically feasible?

studies.name: fig1-architecture
studies.title: Fig 1 — Whole-cell integration: six submodels wired through shared cell variables
studies.question:
Does viva-Mgen actually reproduce Fig 1's central architectural claim — that
the whole-cell model is a set of independent submodels *integrated* through a
shared set of cell variables — as a real, runnable composite rather than a
drawing? Do all six submodels compose, share stores, and run as one integrated
cell?

studies.name: fig2-growth
studies.title: Fig 2 — Cell growth: 9 h doubling time and protein-dominant composition
studies.question:
Does the reduced-but-genuine viva-Mgen cell (FBA metabolism over iPS189
driving mass accumulation) reproduce the trained whole-cell model's core
growth phenotype from Fig 2 — a ~9 h doubling time and a protein-dominant
dry-mass composition?

studies.name: fig3-expression
studies.title: Fig 3 — Chromosome DNA-protein interactions (viva-Mgen)
studies.question:
Does the reduced viva-Mgen expression module (stochastic transcription +
translation + RNA/protein decay on a representative gene panel) reproduce the
qualitative single-cell gene-expression dynamics of Fig 3 / 2G-2H — bursty,
low-copy mRNA alongside protein that accumulates to much higher, more stable
copy numbers (the mRNA↔protein decoupling)?

studies.name: fig4-cell-cycle
studies.title: Fig 4 — Emergent, unregulated control of cell-cycle duration
studies.question:
Does the viva-Mgen replication submodel reproduce Fig 4's central finding —
that M. genitalium's cell-cycle duration is controlled *emergently*, without a
dedicated genetic regulator, through the coupling of replication initiation and
a dNTP surplus that it builds up?

studies.name: fig5-energy
studies.title: Fig 5 — Global distribution of cellular energy: ATP > GTP synthesis and a translation-dominated budget
studies.question:
Does the reduced viva-Mgen cell reproduce Fig 5's global energy picture — that
ATP and GTP are the dominant synthesized carriers with ATP > GTP (Fig 5A), and
that the cellular energy budget is dominated by translation, ahead of
transcription (Fig 5D)?

studies.name: fig6-gene-essentiality
studies.title: Fig 6A — Single-gene-disruption essentiality: model vs experiment
studies.question:
Does the viva-Mgen FBA metabolism submodel reproduce Fig 6A — the
single-gene-disruption essentiality phenotype — for the metabolic genes of
M. genitalium: does an in-silico single-gene knockout predict which genes are
essential, matching the reference essentiality calls?

studies.name: fig7-kinetic-parameters
studies.title: Fig 7E-G — Kinetic parameters: growth depends sigmoidally on an enzyme's kcat (Vmax proxy)
studies.question:
Does the reduced-but-genuine viva-Mgen cell reproduce Fig 7E-G's central
quantitative claim — that predicted growth rate depends on an enzyme's kinetic
parameter (kcat/Vmax), producing a SIGMOIDAL growth-vs-kcat curve that rises
from near-zero at low activity and saturates at the wild-type rate once the
enzyme is no longer rate-limiting?
